extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners handling reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners (and practitioners) on handling, prosecuting, and deciding reissue patent applications, including procedures when related litigation or PTAB proceedings are involved and requirements for reissue oaths/declarations and supplemental submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate IFW for concurrent litigation/PTAB trial
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue application files maintained in the Image File Wrapper (IFW) system, if the existence of litigation or PTAB trial has not already been noted, the examiner should annotate the printed bibliographic data sheet such that adequate notice is provided of the existence of the litigation or PTAB trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure IFW 'Search Notes' or bibliographic forms are annotated to reflect litigation; this provides notice and aids downstream handling. See also instructions to request a litigation search and to scan Search Notes into the reissue application file history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for suspension when litigation arises
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner becomes aware of litigation involving the patent sought to be reissued during examination of the reissue application, the examiner should first check MPEP § 1442.02 to determine whether prosecution in the reissue application should be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution will not be suspended and applicant has not made litigation details of record, inquire in the next Office action. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 14.06) for such inquiries. Consult TQAS/SPRS before suspending (see other entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard reply period during litigation or PTAB trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will normally be given 2 months to reply to Office actions in all reissue applications that are being examined during litigation or PTAB trial, or after litigation or PTAB trial had been stayed, dismissed, etc., to allow for consideration of the reissue by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 2-month period may be extended only upon a showing of clear justification under 37 CFR 1.136(b). The Office action will inform applicant that 37 CFR 1.136(a) extensions are not available. Examiner (with supervisor) may set up to 3 months initially if clearly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to not suspend when specific conditions present (A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the following applies: (A) a stay of the litigation is in effect; (B) the litigation or trial before the PTAB has been terminated; (C) there are no significant overlapping issues between the application and the litigation or pending PTAB trial; or (D) it is applicant’s desire that the application be examined at that time; then the Office may or may not suspend the reissue application using its discretion based upon the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where (A)-(D) apply, form paragraphs 14.08-14.10 may be used to deny suspension (i.e., deny stay). If none apply, action should generally be suspended (use form paragraph 14.11 to stay). Examiner should consult TQAS or SPRS before suspending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form paragraphs to deny or grant stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 14.08–14.11 (and related variations) are used to communicate denials of suspension or to suspend action in reissue applications with concurrent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶14.08 for litigation terminated; ¶14.09 when litigation not overlapping; ¶14.10 when applicant requests examination; ¶14.11 to stay action in view of concurrent litigation. Use appropriate paragraph text to explain that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted due to litigation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination merged with reissue is not stayed by litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination proceeding will not be stayed where there is litigation. Thus, where a reissue application has been merged with an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the merged proceeding will not be stayed because of litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In merged ex parte reexamination/reissue proceedings, ex parte reexamination controls due to 35 U.S.C. 305 requirement for special dispatch. See MPEP §§ 2285, 2286. For merges with inter partes reexamination, see 37 CFR 1.937 and MPEP § 2686.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing for reissue applications with stayed litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications, except those under suspension because of litigation, will be taken up for action ahead of other 'special' applications; reissue applications involved in 'stayed litigation' will be taken up in advance of other reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is placed on expedited processing where courts expect expedited treatment. The Office will entertain petitions under 37 CFR 1.182 (with fee under 1.17(f)) to not apply the 2‑month delay period. TQAS/SPRS oversight, monthly status reports from each Technology Center, and time-monitoring systems are used to track progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to waive 2‑month delay for stayed litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In reissue applications with 'stayed litigation,' the Office will entertain petitions under 37 CFR 1.182, accompanied by the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f), to not apply the 2‑month delay period stated in MPEP § 1441.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions are decided by the Office of Patent Legal Administration. Use form paragraph 14.07 for actions where litigation is stayed but reissue is not stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify Office of prior or concurrent proceedings (applicant obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any reissue application before the Office, the applicant must call to the attention of the Office any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences or PTAB trials, reissues, reexaminations, litigations) and the results of such proceedings (see 37 CFR 1.178(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification should be at time of, or shortly after, filing—either in the reissue oath/declaration or in a separate paper accompanying the application. Litigation begun after filing should also be promptly brought to the Office's attention. Include sufficient information for the Office to evaluate need for further materials; describe and preferably submit supporting materials substantiating allegations of invalidity, but avoid voluminous irrelevant litigation materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as litigation (scope of materials applicant should provide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Litigation encompasses any papers filed in the court or issued by the court, including motions, pleadings, court decisions, and results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying the Office of litigation, submit enough information for the Office to evaluate relevance; include a description (and preferably copies) of supporting materials that substantiate allegations relevant to reissue patentability. Examiners may request copies of papers and records in suits or ask the Office of the Solicitor to obtain them when not otherwise obtainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should request litigation search and annotate records
rubrics_metrics.description: A litigation search should be requested by the examiner to determine whether the patent has been, or is, involved in litigation. For IFW reissue application files, the 'Search Notes' box on the 'Search Notes' form is annotated to indicate that the review was conducted, and the 'Search Notes' form is scanned into the reissue application file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the examiner becomes aware of litigation and applicant has not made details of record, the examiner should inquire in the next Office action (form paragraph 14.06) and may request further materials if material to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examiner review of chain of title and consent under 37 CFR 1.172
rubrics_metrics.description: On initial receipt, the examiner should inspect the submission under 37 CFR 1.172 as to documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee to determine whether the consent requirement of 37 CFR 1.172 has been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the consent and documentary evidence of ownership; the assignee indicated by the documentary evidence must be the same assignee who signed the consent. The person who signs the consent and the person who signs the submission of evidence of ownership must both have authority. If assignment document is referenced by reel/frame and supports the statement, a copy is not necessary. If assigned but documentary evidence absent, require submission using form paragraph 14.16. If applicant states not assigned and Office records do not cast doubt, no submission is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette announcement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of all reissue applications, except for continued prosecution applications (CPAs) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), must be announced in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check Patent Data Portal Content History for 'NRE' and 'NOTICE OF REISSUE PUBLISHED IN OFFICIAL GAZETTE' entries and the publication date. If not announced, return jurisdiction to Office of Patent Application Processing (Special Processing) to handle the announcement. Examiner should not further act on the reissue until 2 months after announcement (see MPEP § 1440).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify concurrent procedural statuses and file hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should determine if there is concurrent litigation (and status), whether the reissue file history is appropriately marked, whether a protest has been filed, whether the patent is involved in an interference, whether certificate of correction changes have been incorporated, and whether the patent has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP §§ 1442.01, 1404, 1901.06, 1449.01, 1411.01, and 1415.01 as appropriate. TQAS or SPRS is responsible for oversight of reissue applications with related litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner must personally review sufficiency of reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of the sufficiency of the reissue oath/declaration filed under 37 CFR 1.175 must in each case be reviewed and decided personally by the primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much required content differs based on filing date, but all reissue oaths/declarations must contain (A) a statement that applicant believes original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid (by reason of defective specification/drawing or claiming more or less than right) and (B) a statement of at least one error relied upon to support the reissue. See MPEP § 1414 and subsections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject claims when reissue oath/declaration fails 37 CFR 1.175(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reissue oath/declaration fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.175(a), the examiner will so notify applicant in an Office action, rejecting the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In preparing an Office action, use form paragraphs 14.01 through 14.01.06 to state objections to the oath/declaration and form paragraph 14.14 to reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 based on improper oath/declaration. If unsigned (except in limited exceptions), the oath/declaration is insufficient and leads to rejection; but if unsigned oath submitted as part of a reply otherwise properly signed, accept the reply and address the oath in the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when initially-identified errors are no longer relied upon — post‑Sept‑16‑2012 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration is not required where all errors previously identified are no longer being relied upon; however, the applicant must explicitly identify an error being relied upon as the basis for reissue (e.g., in the remarks accompanying an amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the error must be conspicuous and clear and must comply with 35 U.S.C. 251. Applicant is not required to identify the new error in a reissue oath/declaration, but identification may not be deferred until allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when initially-identified errors are no longer relied upon — pre‑Sept‑16‑2012 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012, where all prior errors identified are no longer relied upon, a supplemental oath/declaration will be needed to identify at least one error now being relied upon as the basis for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental oath/declaration is not required to indicate that earlier errors are no longer being corrected. Applicant may defer submission of the supplemental oath/declaration until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance; such a request may be treated as a complete reply to the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reissue oath/declaration requirements (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental oath/declaration under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) must be submitted before allowance and will be required where: (A) the application is otherwise in condition for allowance; (B) amendments or other corrections of errors were made subsequent to the last oath/declaration; and (C) at least one amendment corrects an error under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When required, examiner is encouraged to telephone applicant to request submission. If applicant cannot or will not promptly submit it, the examiner should issue a final Office action (final rejection) and use form paragraph 14.05.02.fti. Examples of acceptable language for the supplemental oath/declaration are provided in MPEP § 1414.01 and form paragraph guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 14.05.02.fti and guidance for its application
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 14.05.02.fti is used in an Office action to remind applicant of the requirement for submission of the supplemental reissue oath/declaration under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) before allowance and to reject all claims since the reissue application is defective until submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this form paragraph in applications filed on or after September 16, 2012. Do not use if no amendments correcting errors were made after last oath/rejection; instead allow the case. This paragraph cannot be used in an Ex parte Quayle action to require the supplemental oath/declaration. Do not use in an examiner's amendment; the supplemental oath/declaration must be filed prior to mailing of the Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections after allowance must follow 37 CFR 1.312 and justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant seeks to correct an error after allowance, any amendment of the patent correcting the error must be submitted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.312; no amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments under 1.312 must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee and may be entered upon recommendation of the primary examiner and approval of the supervisory patent examiner. Remarks accompanying such amendments must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier. For pre‑2012 reissue applications, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration must accompany the amendment after allowance if correcting an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application examined same as non‑reissue application; no presumption of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application, including all the claims therein, is to be examined in the same manner as a non‑reissue, non‑provisional application. Claims in a reissue application enjoy no 'presumption of validity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are subject to any and all rejections the examiner deems appropriate regardless of identity to patent claims or prior prosecution history. Prior prosecution of the patent does not prevent rejections in the reissue application.
